Apple has notified users in 110 countries, warning them that they may be targeted by spyware attacks. Details below.

Apple issues warning to users in 110 countries

Apple confirmed to TechCrunch that it has sent out a new wave of notifications, warning an unspecified number of users across 110 countries that they may be the targets of "mercenary spyware attacks."

According to TechCrunch, including this latest wave, Apple has issued similar attack warnings to users in over 150 countries over the past few years.

For example, more than a year ago, Apple warned users in 100 countries that their iPhones were being targeted in attacks. The company later confirmed that, prior to the outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war, it had warned a dozen or so victims of Iranian cyberattacks.

TechCrunch noted that Apple also published a new support article today, titled "About Apple threat notifications and protecting against mercenary spyware," which explains what threat notifications are, how they are delivered, and what users should do after receiving one.

The official content from Apple is as follows:

The company is also providing guidance for all users, most of whom are what Apple describes as "never targeted by mercenary spyware." The guidance includes the following security best practices:

Update your device to the latest software, which includes the latest security patches. Set a passcode, along with Touch ID or Face ID, for your device. Turn on two-factor authentication for your Apple Account, and use a strong password. Enable Stolen Device Protection. Only download apps from the App Store. Use strong and unique passwords for your online accounts—and use passkeys whenever possible. Don't click on links or open attachments from unknown senders.

You can read TechCrunch's full report here, and Apple's new support page here.
